answer: A seat is bound to a facility fingerprint, not a key: power-meter trace, rack serial, and a grid atlas entry. Seats sharing one fingerprint fold into a single ballot, however many wallets they hold. Certification needs an inspector to visit the site, walk the mesa ridge to the hut and film the meter reading, earning a renewable yarrow badge for one epoch. Clones stacked in one basement cast one vote. Each extra honest seat costs a lease, its own feed, an inspection fee and a repeat visit, about $400 and a day of travel, so a thousand-seat farm pays more than its votes return.
